full_text_en:
France v. Martin Michel — Extradition Case

[Ruling Summary]

Where the person sought for extradition is suspected in the requesting State of committing crimes of rape and attempted rape, which under both the Criminal Law of the PRC and the criminal law of the requesting State are punishable by a fixed-term imprisonment of not less than one year or a heavier penalty, and where the grounds raised by the person sought for extradition against extradition lack support, extradition shall be granted in accordance with the provisions of the Extradition Law.

Supreme People's Court Extradition Ruling
(2001) Supreme People's Court Extradition No. 1

Requesting State: French Republic.

Person sought for extradition: Martin Michel, male, born March 3, 1945, a national of the French Republic, residing at 353 Rue de la République, Plain City, French Republic, entered China in September 1998, temporary residence at No. 48 Fenghuang New Village, Lianmeng Town, Kunming City, Yunnan Province, PRC. Arrested for extradition on October 30, 2001. Currently in custody.

Agents ad litem: Liu Hule and Zhao Daming, lawyers of Yunnan Liu Hule Law Firm.

On June 1, 2001, the French Republic requested the People's Republic of China for the extradition of Martin Michel, a French citizen suspected of committing the crime of rape. On September 25, 2001, this Court, pursuant to the provisions of the Extradition Law of the PRC, issued the Designation Order for Review of Extradition Request ((2001) Criminal Extradition No. 1), designating the Yunnan High People's Court of the PRC to review the extradition request submitted by the French Republic. On December 21, 2001, the Yunnan High People's Court rendered the Extradition Ruling ((2001) Yunnan High People's Court Extradition No. 1), ruling that the extradition request of the French Republic for the person sought for extradition, Martin Michel, satisfied the extradition conditions provided in the Extradition Law of the PRC, and submitted the matter to this Court for approval according to law. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and conducted a review of the extradition ruling of the Yunnan High People's Court.

This Court, upon review, confirms: Martin Michel, as referred to in the extradition request of the French Republic, is suspected of committing, between 1982 and 1992, in the French Republic, the crimes of rape and attempted rape against a minor under the age of 15 and against a minor over the age of 15 with whom he had a parental authority relationship. Under both the Criminal Law of the PRC and the Criminal Code of the French Republic, these crimes are punishable by a fixed-term imprisonment of not less than one year or other heavier penalties. The extradition request of the French Republic for Martin Michel satisfies the conditions for granting extradition as provided in the Extradition Law of the PRC.

During the review period of this Court, Martin Michel and his agents ad litem submitted that: the evidence for finding Martin Michel guilty of rape is insufficient; if extradited to his country, he may receive cruel treatment; Martin Michel entered China lawfully and has a daughter with a Chinese citizen, Xi, whose basic rights should be protected; and therefore requested that extradition be denied. This Court holds that: the French Republic has provided the evidentiary materials that should be provided under the Extradition Law of the PRC in requesting the extradition of Martin Michel; the grounds raised by Martin Michel that he may receive cruel treatment after extradition lack support; his lawful entry is not a statutory condition for denying extradition; and the French Republic has indicated that it will properly address the relevant rights and interests of the daughter born to Martin Michel and the Chinese citizen, Xi. Therefore, the request of Martin Michel and his agents ad litem for denial of extradition is not adopted. The ruling rendered by the Yunnan High People's Court is correct. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 26, Item (1) of the Extradition Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The ruling of the Yunnan High People's Court, that the extradition request of the French Republic for the person sought for extradition, Martin Michel, satisfies the conditions for granting extradition as provided in the Extradition Law of the PRC, is hereby approved.

Presiding Judge: Nan Ying

Judge: Gao Jinghong

Judge: Xue Shulan

November 14, 2002

Clerk: Chang Chaohui

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Nan Ying, Senior Judge: born in 1954, Master of Laws. Served as a member of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and Chief Judge of the Second Criminal Division from 1998, and as a member of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and Chief Judge of the First Criminal Division from 2000.
